record.original_question: Develop general methods for proving the existence of local minimizers of the elastic energy I that are not global minimizers, and for proving the existence of other weak solutions of the equilibrium equations, including equilibrium solutions that are not local minimizers.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. Devise general methods for proving the existence of local minimizers of I that are not global minimizers, and of other weak solutions of the equilibrium equations.
How can one prove the existence of equilibrium solutions that are not local minimizers?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain (with $n=2$ or $n=3$) representing the reference configuration of a hyperelastic body. For deformations $y:\Omega 	o \mathbb{R}^n$ in a suitable Sobolev class (for instance $y \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^n)$ for some $p \geq 1$, possibly subject to boundary conditions on a part of $\partial\Omega$ and to the local invertibility constraint $\det 
abla y(x) > 0$ a.e.), consider the elastic energy functional
$$ I(y) = \int_{\Omega} W(x, 
abla y(x))\, dx, $$
where the stored-energy density $W:\Omega 	imes \mathbb{R}^{n	imes n}_+ 	o \mathbb{R}$ is frame-indifferent, polyconvex (or otherwise of the type used in nonlinear elasticity), and satisfies $W(x,F) 	o \infty$ as $\det F 	o 0^+$.

A deformation $y^*$ is a weak solution of the equilibrium equations if it is a critical point of $I$ in an appropriate variational sense, i.e.
$$ \int_{\Omega}  rac{\partial W}{\partial F}(x, 
abla y^*) : 
abla \varphi\, dx = 0 $$
for all admissible variations $\varphi$. It is a local minimizer (with respect to a chosen topology, e.g. $L^1$, $L^\infty$, or $W^{1,p}$) if $I(y^*) \le I(y)$ for all admissible $y$ sufficiently close to $y^*$ in that topology, and a global minimizer if $I(y^*) \le I(y)$ for all admissible $y$.

Develop general methods to establish:
(a) the existence of local minimizers of $I$ that are not global minimizers; and
(b) the existence of weak solutions of the equilibrium equations that are not local minimizers of $I$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is one of John Ball's well-known open problems in nonlinear elasticity (Problem 9 in his list of open problems). General methods for producing non-global local minimizers and non-minimizing critical points of the elasticity functional remain a long-standing open challenge; only partial results in special geometries (e.g., via mountain-pass, symmetry-breaking, or bifurcation arguments) are available. No general method is known.
